The importance of the services provided by the proposed facility to the
community.
The requirements of the facility for a waterfront location.
The availability of alternative locations not subject to flooding for the
proposed use.
The compatibility of the proposed use with existing development and
development anticipated in the foreseeable future.
The relationship of the proposed use to the comprehensive plan and
floodplain management program for the area.
The safety of access by ordinary and emergency vehicles to the property
in time of flood.
The expected heights, velocity, duration, rate of rise, and sediment
transport of the floodwaters expected at the site.
The repair or rehabilitation of historic structures upon a determination
that the proposed repair or rehabilitation will not preclude the
structure's continued designation as a historic structure and the
variance is the minimum necessary to preserve the historic character
and design of the structure.
Such other factors which are relevant to the purposes of this overlay
district.
The BZA may refer any application and accompanying documentation
pertaining to any request for a variance to any engineer or other qualified
person or agency for technical assistance in evaluating the proposed project
in relation to flood heights or velocities and the adequacy of the plans for
flood protection and other related matters.
Required Findings
Variances shall be issued only after the BZA has determined that the variance
will be the minimum required to provide relief and that the granting of such
will not result in any of the following:
Unacceptable or prohibited increases in flood heights;
Additional threats to public safety;
Extraordinary public expense;

3.9.8 HO: Historic Overlay

Any nuisance;
Fraud or victimization of the public; or
Conflict with local laws or ordinances.
Notification
The BZA shall notify the applicant for a variance, in writing, that the issuance
of a variance to construct a structure below the BFE or flood depth:
Will increase the risks to life and property; and
Will result in increased premium rates for flood insurance or the
inability to obtain flood insurance through the NFIP.
A record shall be maintained of the above notification as well as all approved
variances from the provisions of this overlay district, including justification
for the issuance of each variance. Any variances that are issued shall be
noted in the annual or biennial report submitted to the Federal Insurance
Administrator.

sections.title: HO: Historic Overlay
sections.text:
PURPOSE
The purpose of the Historic Overlay (HO) district is to protect and conserve
individual historic buildings, structures, and areas located outside of an Historic
and Cultural Conservation (HC) district in order to achieve the historic
preservation objectives and policies in the comprehensive plan.
APPLICABILITY
General Applicability
The standards and requirements in this section apply to individually-
designated HO districts, in addition to the base zoning district requirements.
Specific Areas of Applicability
Specific HO districts will be listed below as they are established by the city.
Those established to date include:
The Downtown Historic Overlay (HO – Downtown) district (see Section
3.9.8.E(1));
The Norfolk & Western Historic Overlay (HO – N&W) district (see
Section 3.9.8.E(2))
District Boundaries
Individual HO districts shall be represented on the Official Zoning Map.
DESIGN GUIDELINE S
Prior to development in an HO district, a developer shall receive approval of a
Certificate of Appropriateness, in accordance with Section 2.4.10., Certificate of

Appropriateness, and any additional design guidelines as established by the
Architectural Review Board.
REQUIRED MAINTE NANCE
All buildings and structures within a HO district shall be maintained as provided in
Section 3.6.4. Standards Applicable to All Historic and Cultural Conservation Base
Zoning Districts.
SPECIFIC HISTORIC OVERLAY DISTRICTS
The following HO districts have been established:
HO – Downtown: Downtown Historic Overlay
Purpose Statement
The purpose of the Downtown Historic Overlay (HO-Downtown) district
is to protect buildings and sites in downtown Norfolk that reflect
culturally-significant commercial architectural styles of the late-19th
through mid-20th centuries. The district is intended to:
Preserve and enhance compatible and harmonious architectural
styles that give the district its distinct character;
Protect significant structures and sites, which include sites listed on
the National Register of Historic Places, from destruction;
Encourage uses and activities which will foster their conservation
and improvement;
Prevent the creation or encroachment of adverse influences from
adjacent lands; and
Ensure new structures and uses within the district are compatible
with the district’s character.
HO – N&W: Norfolk & Western Historic Overlay
Purpose Statement
The purpose of the Norfolk & Western Historic Overlay (HO – N&W)
district is to protect buildings and sites located along the historic
Norfolk & Western railway and within the boundaries of either the
Norfolk & Western Railroad (DHR No.: 122-5799) or the Williamston-
Woodland (DHR No.: 122-5795) historic districts, as listed on the State
and National Register of Historic Places by the Virginia Department of
Historic Resources and the National Park Service. The intent of the HO –
N&W district is to preserve the historic development pattern of the light
industrial building stock, allow for flexibility in reuse due to the changing
requirements for operators of industrial businesses, and to ensure that
new construction and renovations are harmonious with the industrial
character. District standards are intended to promote a vibrant mixed-

3.9.8 HO: Historic Overlay

use environment which will accommodate the current and changing use
patterns.
Eligibility for Rezoning
At the time of the creation of this overlay district, no properties are
zoned or rezoned to lie within the district. To be included in the overlay
district, a map amendment must be approved (see Section 2.4.3, Zoning
Map Amendment). No property is eligible to be rezoned to this overlay
district except those which are already included in either the Norfolk &
Western Railroad or the Williamston-Woodland historic districts
(identified in subsection (a), above) at the time the rezoning application
is filed.
Review Procedures
A Development Certificate (see Sections 2.3.3, Development Certificate
Review Procedure, and 2.4.9, Development Certificate) shall be
obtained prior to the issuance of any Zoning Certificate for new
principal structures, and substantial improvements to existing
structures in the HO – N&W district, in accordance with the definition of
“substantial improvement” which exempts historic structures (see
Section 8.3.2).
Adaptive Re-use
In addition to any use allowed as either a permitted or conditional use
within the base zoning district, any use listed in either Table 3.2.12 or
Table 3.3.9 of this ordinance may be permitted in a building designated
within a HO – N&W district if approved by a Conditional Use Permit.
Yard Requirements
The following minimum yard setbacks may be reduced from the
minimum setback requirements of the base zoning district as follows:
Front Yard, Side Yard and Corner Side Yard
May be reduced to match an adjacent building setback or a
reduced setback for a building located either across the street or
diagonally across an intersection.
Off-Street Parking Requirements
Residential development of 24 dwelling units or fewer on a single
zoning lot shall not be required to provide off-street parking.
Residential development of more than 24 dwelling units shall
provide the minimum number of off-street parking spaces set forth
in Table 5.1.7(D), Minimum Number of Parking Spaces. For
purposes of determining the number of required off-street parking
spaces, all units included in the development shall be counted.

Non-residential development shall not be required to provide off-
street parking.

sections.title: BCRO: Broad Creek Refresh Overlay
sections.text:
PURPOSE STATEMENT
The purpose of the Broad Creek Refresh Overlay (BCRO) district is to promote
neighborhood-supportive uses and a mixture of residential uses that reflect the
existing housing stock variety and promote new housing opportunities in a
manner that is consistent with the Broad Creek Refresh Plan: Building a
Community of Choice. The district also intends to protect and preserve unique
design features and community character within the Broad Creek area by
promoting development that is compatible with existing neighborhood character
and the Traditional Character District.
APPLICABILITY
The standards and requirements in this section apply to all new development in
the BCRO district in addition to the Form Standards applicable to the Traditional
Character District. Where these standards conflict with any general form
standard listed in Table 5.9.3, Single-Family Detached Dwellings Form Standards,
these more specific standards shall be applied instead of the general form
standard, except as specified separately below.
DEVELOPMENT AND PERFORMANCE STANDARDS
Alterations to Standards From Base Zoning Districts
The following development and performance standards that would
otherwise apply under the applicable regulations of the base zoning district
are altered in the BCRO district as follows:
Notwithstanding anything in Section 2.3.6, Administrative Review
Procedure, to the contrary, no fence or wall shall be installed prior to
receipt of a Zoning Certificate approving the installation.
No Conditional Use Permit shall be required for any Live-Work Dwelling
within the Bruce’s Park Neighborhood Core or Greater Bruce’s Park
areas, as described in Section 3.9.9.F(1) below, except where the non-
residential use proposed to be a part of the live-work dwelling would
otherwise require a Conditional Use Permit.
A Conditional Use Permit is required for any development of more than
12 multi-family dwelling units.
A Conditional Use Permit is required for any development of any
Townhouse Dwelling.
Development Standards for All Residential Development
The following development standards apply to any property within the BRCO
district that has a base zoning district of SF-T, MF-NS, C-N, or C-C:

3.9.9 BCRO: Broad Creek Refresh Overlay

Building Orientation
On any corner lot, the primary entrance of the principal building shall
face the same street that is faced by most buildings located along the
two block faces along which the corner lot is situated.
Building Height
No structure shall be more than 3 stories in height. The following
structures are exempt from this restriction and have no height limit
different than is applicable for the base zoning district in which each it
located:
Any single-family home
Principal buildings fronting East Princess Anne Road
Principal buildings fronting East Virginia Beach Boulevard
Principal buildings fronting Ballentine Boulevard
Principal buildings fronting Park Avenue
Principal buildings fronting Corprew Avenue
Attached Garage
Every attached garage must be constructed of materials that are
compatible with the principal structure.
Every side-loaded attached garage shall have an entrance that does
not face the same street as the primary entrance of the principal
building. The front façade of the attached garage shall have
architectural treatments compatible with those on the front
façade.
Accessory Structures
Except on corner lots and through lots, every accessory structure
shall be located entirely behind the rearmost portion of the
principal building.
Every detached garage must be constructed of materials that are
compatible with the principal structure on the same lot.
Driveways
Except on corner lots, no portion of a driveway shall be located in that
portion of the lot between the front façade of the principal building and
the front property line.
Roofs
No flat roofs shall be permitted on any single-family dwelling except
when such roof is over an attached porch or other addition to the
principal structure.

Fences and Walls
Opaque fences shall not extend anywhere on the lot that is nearer
to the front yard than the nearest rear corner of the principal
structure.
Any fence located in any interior side yard shall not exceed six (6)
feet in height and no more than the lowest four (4) feet of any such
fence may be opaque.
Chain link fencing is prohibited within the front yard and corner
side yard.
Variability
If multiple new residences are developed on adjacent lots or on the
same block face, the ZA shall require that any contiguous set of three or
more parcels shall include at least two variants from The Traditional
Neighborhoods Plan Book or the Missing Middle Pattern Book, as
applicable.
Alternative Approval for Certain Development Standards
The front porch dimensions for a single-family dwelling otherwise required
under Section 5.9.3, Single-Family Detached Dwellings Form Standards, may
be altered to conform to an alternative building design that has been
approved by the ARB pursuant to the process set forth in Section 2.3.4,
Architectural Review Board Procedure, provided that the ARB determines
that the proposed design is consistent with the designs identified for
“Traditional Broad Creek” described in The Broad Creek Refresh: A Pattern
Book (Appendix to the General Plan of Norfolk).
FORM AND DESIG N STANDARDS FOR NON -RESIDENTIAL
DEVELOPMENT
The following regulations apply to any any property within the BRCO district that
has a commercial or industrial base zoning district.
No off-street loading berth shall be situated facing any of the following
streets:
East Princess Anne Road
East Virginia Beach Boulevard
Ballentine Boulevard
Park Avenue
Corprew Avenue
PROHIBITED USES
The uses listed in Table 3.9.9 are prohibited within the BCRO district:

3.9.9 BCRO: Broad Creek Refresh Overlay

TABLE 3.9.9: PROHIBITED USES WITHIN THE BCRO
DISTRICT
PRINCIPAL USES
Check cashing, auto title, or payday loan businesses
Convenience store
Novelty store or theater, adult
Pawnshop
Smoke or vape shop
Automobile repair and maintenance, major
Automobile repair and maintenance, minor
Automobile rental
Automobile sales
Boat sales, rental, service, or repair
Car wash
Gas station
Recreational vehicle sale, rental, and maintenance
Taxi or limousine service facilities
Tire sales and repair
BASE DISTRICTS
Automatic car wash
Drive-through facility, large-scale
Gasoline sales (as an accessory use)
Sale of smoking or vaping products
DEVELOPMENT ST ANDARDS FOR BR UCE’S PARK
The following standards are intended to prevent residential development that is
inconsistent with the unique form and development pattern of the Traditional
Character District and any benefits of housing choice and walkability provided by
Missing Middle Housing.
Specific Areas of Applicability
Respecting the existing, varying lot patterns in the Bruce’s Park
neighborhood, two distinct areas that may be regulated using different
development standards, are identified and delineated as follows:
Bruce’s Park Neighborhood Core – generally bounded as follows:
On the north by Cary Avenue and that portion of Goff Street west
of Hanson Avenue;
On the south by East Princess Anne Road;
On the east by Majestic Avenue; and

On the west by Courtney Avenue
Greater Bruce’s Park – generally bounded as follows:
On the north by the Virginia Department of Rail and Public
Transportation railroad right-of-way lying parallel to and south of
Saint Julian Avenue;
On the south by Cary Avenue and that portion of Goff Street west
of Hanson Avenue;
On the east by Roberts Road; and
On the west by the Norfolk Southern railroad right-of-way lying

parallel with and east of Tidewater Drive.

3.9.9 BCRO: Broad Creek Refresh Overlay

Approval Process
Zoning Certificate Required
Any proposed development that meets all standards set forth in this
subsection (2) shall be permitted upon receipt of a Zoning Certificate
issued in accordance with Section 2.4.14, Zoning Certificate.
Conditional Use Permit Required
Any development that does not meet all the standards set forth in this
subsection (2) may per permitted upon grant of a Conditional Use
Permit reviewed in accordance with Section 2.4.8, Conditional Use
Permit, provided that such Permit authorizes a reduction in any of the
intensity or dimensional standards expressly allowed in this section.
General Design Criteria
The development of all structures on the lot must satisfy either of the
following criteria:
Pattern and Plan Books
The design, massing, location, and arrangement of the structures
conform to the guidelines set forth in the Missing Middle Pattern
Book (Appendix B to the General Plan of Norfolk) or any of the
house plans shown in the “Traditional Neighborhoods Plan Book.”
Architectural Review Board
The design, massing, location, and arrangement of the structures
has been reviewed and approved by the ARB pursuant to the
process set forth in Section 2.2.4, Architectural Review Board,
provided that the ARB determines that the proposed development
is consistent with the guidelines set forth in the Missing Middle
Pattern Book (Appendix B to the General Plan of Norfolk).
Uses
The lot shall only be used for one or more of the following uses:
Single-family detached dwelling
Single-family semi-detached dwelling
Two-family dwelling
Multi-family dwelling with no more than six (6) dwelling units.
Accessory dwelling unit, with the following additional permissions
and performance standards:
(A) Such units shall be accessory only to a single-family detached
dwelling, a single-family semi-detached dwelling, or a
townhouse dwelling.

(B) Such units are not required to meet the standards in Section
4.3.3.E(1)(a)(ii) regarding minimum area, dimensional, and lot
coverage standards of the zoning district in which it is located.
(C) Such units shall not exceed 600 square feet in area.
On any lot located in the Greater Bruce’s Park specific areas of
applicability, defined and delineated in subsection (1), above,
Multi-family dwellings with no more than 12 dwelling units
Parking
The maximum number of parking spaces permitted shall be 1 space
per dwelling unit.
No minimum number of parking spaces are required for any single-
family dwelling (detached or attached), two-family dwelling, or
multi-family dwelling with no more than three (3) dwelling units.
The minimum number of required parking spaces for any multi-
family dwelling with four (4) to six (6) units shall be two (2) parking
spaces.
The minimum number of required parking spaces for any multi-
family dwelling with seven (7) or eight (8) units shall be four (4)
parking spaces.
The minimum number of required parking spaces for any multi-
family dwelling with nine (9) to twelve (12) units shall be five (5)
parking spaces.
Alternative Parking Plan
The ZA is authorized to approve an alternative parking plan, in
accordance with the standards of Section 5.1.7.C, Alternative
Parking, that proposes a fewer number of parking spaces than
what is required above. The alternative parking plan shall propose
a strategy that will effectively reduce parking demand on the site in
a way that will do at least as good a job in protecting surrounding
neighborhoods, maintaining traffic-circulation patterns, and
promoting quality urban design, stormwater management, and
biophilic design as would strict compliance with the otherwise
applicable off-street parking standards.
Yard Requirements
For all uses listed in subsection (d), above, the minimum side yard
setback shall be three (3) feet.

3.9.10 PCO: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay

sections.title: PCO: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay
sections.text:
PURPOSE
The purpose of the Pedestrian Commercial Overlay (PCO) district is to encourage
the compatible mixing of commercial land uses in a pedestrian-oriented
development pattern. The district is also intended to maintain and enhance
existing and planned pedestrian amenities and infrastructure that supports the
district’s pedestrian-oriented character.
APPLICABILITY
The standards in this section apply to individually-designated PCO districts.
There are five PCO districts, each of which their own development standards
and requirements:
PCO-Colley: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-Colley Avenue (see Section
3.9.11).
PCO-21st Street: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-21st Street (see
Section 3.9.12)
PCO-Riverview: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-Riverview (see Section
3.9.13).
PCO-35th Street: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-35th Street (see
Section 3.9.14).
PCO-Lafayette: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-Lafayette Boulevard
(see Section 3.9.15).
Individual PCO districts shall be identified on the Official Zoning Map so that
principal pedestrian commercial street frontage and supporting parking
areas are included.
REVIEW PROCEDURES APPLICABLE T O ALL PCO
DISTRICTS
A Development Certificate (see Section 2.4.9, Development Certificate) shall be
obtained prior to the issuance of any Zoning Certificate for new principal
structures and substantial improvements or additions to existing principal
structures in a PCO district.
DEVELOPMENT ST ANDARDS APPLICABLE TO ALL PCO
DISTRICTS
The ZA may determine applicable build-to or setback lines on corner lots in all
PCO districts, taking into consideration the average build-to or setback lines of
existing development on the same block face.

sections.title: PCO-Colley: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-Colley Avenue
sections.text:
AVENUE
PURPOSE
The purpose of the Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-Colley Avenue (PCO-Colley)
district to maintain and enhance the commercial vitality and pedestrian character
of the Colley Avenue business area and reinforce the existing concentration of
pedestrian-oriented commercial establishments. District standards accommodate
development that is harmonious with the district’s character.
APPLICABILITY
The standards in this section apply to all development in the PCO-Colley district.
STANDARDS APPLICAB LE TO DEVELOPMENT IN PCO -
COLLEY
Building Location and Orientation
The front façade of a building developed on a lot abutting Colley Avenue or
21st Street shall be located within five feet of the front property line. The
primary entrance to the building shall be on Colley Avenue or 21st Street.
Facade Treatment
A minimum of 50 percent of the total area of ground floor facades along
Colley Avenue and 21st Street shall be transparent from the street.
Parking Location and Access
Where the depth of the lot permits, off-street parking shall be located
behind the building(s) and shall have access/egress only from the side
street(s). Rear entrances to the building(s) shall be provided.
In situations where the depth of the lot does not permit parking in the
rear, off-street parking may be located along Colley Avenue provided
only one curb cut not exceeding 20 feet is installed on Colley Avenue.
Another curb cut may be installed on a side street.
A wall or hedge three feet in height shall be located along the Colley
Avenue property line of the parking lot in order to define the edge of
the pedestrian corridor.
Off-street Loading
No off-street loading berth shall be located on Colley Avenue or 21st Street.
Landscaping and Buffering
Except where precluded by the provisions of this district, the landscaping
and buffering standards applicable to commercial uses in Section 5.2,
Landscaping Standards, shall apply.

3.9.11 PCO-Colley: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-Colley Avenue

Signs
Sign standards for commercial uses in Section 5.7, Signs, shall apply, subject
to the following:
Freestanding signs are prohibited.
Only one A-frame sign may be placed on a public sidewalk in front of a
business, which shall be removed from the public right-of-way during
non-business hours. It shall be subject to any other conditions specified
by the ZA to ensure it is designed and located to maintain district
character.
Temporary balloons are prohibited.
Box wall signs, which are geometric in form, plastic coated, internally
lighted, and have a changeable face for each subsequent tenant, are
prohibited.
Wall signs shall comply with the following standards:
They shall complement the building's architecture, materials, and
colors;
One square foot of sign surface area is allowed for each foot of
building frontage facing the public street on which principal access
is located;
One-half square foot of sign surface area is allowed for each foot of
building frontage facing other streets;
Wall signs may include, but are not limited to, the following
features:
(A) Individual articulated letters.
(B) Painted signs (on the building or on other suitable surface).
(C) Neon tubing.
(D) Lettering on an awning.
Digital window signage shall be permitted subject to the following
limitations:
Notwithstanding any other provisions of this subsection, the
transparency required in Section 3.9.11.C(2), Façade Treatment,
must be maintained;
One digital window sign may be permitted per storefront facing a
street. One additional digital window sign may be permitted for
any storefront fronting more than 100 linear feet on a public
street;
Signage shall be no larger than nine square feet;

Signage shall be installed a minimum of three feet off the ground
and no higher than nine feet from the ground;
Display must stay on screen a minimum of 10 seconds and can
change only by fading to the new display;
Display cannot flash, or give the appearance of flashing;
Display may be interactive, but cannot scroll or move unless being
manipulated by a user standing in front of the display;
If digital window signage is used, no temporary window signage
shall be permitted;
No exterior sound shall be emitted from the sign;
Digital window signage shall not cause glare or be lit in a way that
causes a distraction to vehicular traffic; and
No content on the digital widow sign shall be legible from the
vehicular travel lanes of adjacent streets.
Parking Standards
Off-street parking shall comply with Table 3.9.11, Off-street Parking
Standards.

3.9.12 PCO-21st Street: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-21st Street

sections.title: PCO-21st Street: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-21st Street
sections.text:
STREET
PURPOSE
The purpose of the Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-21st Street (PCO-21st Street)
district is to maintain and enhance the commercial vitality and walkable character
of the 21st Street business area and establish a concentration of pedestrian-
oriented commercial establishments. District standards accommodate
development that is harmonious with the district’s walkable character and
planned public improvements.
APPLICABILITY
The standards in this section apply to all development in the PCO-21st Street
district.
STANDARDS APPLICABLE TO DEVEL OPMENT IN THE PC O-
21 S T STREET DISTRICT
Building Location and Orientation
Lots Abutting Colley Avenue, Colonial Avenue, or Llewellyn Avenue
The front façade of a building developed on a lot abutting Colley
Avenue, Colonial Avenue, or Llewellyn Avenue shall be located within
five feet of the front property line. The primary entrance to the
buildings shall be on Colley Avenue, Colonial Avenue, or Llewellyn
Avenue.
Lots Abutting 21st Street or 22nd Street
A building developed on a lot abutting 21st Street or 22nd Street shall
be located in one of the following configurations:
The entire front building facade shall be located 10 feet from the
front property line. The primary entrances to such buildings shall
be on 21st Street or 22nd Street; or
The building orientation shall be perpendicular to 21st Street or
22nd Street with its principal facade and entrances facing a
pedestrian plaza or parking court. In addition, the ends of the
building shall be located between the front property line and 10
feet from the front property line, and shall have active uses and
entrances on the 21st Street or 22nd Street.
In no case shall the building be located in the middle or rear of the
lot with parking or on-site circulation between the building and the
property line on 21st Street or 22nd Street.

3.9.12 PCO-21st Street: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-21st Street

Façade Treatment
A minimum of 50 percent of the total area of ground floor facades along 21st
Street, 22nd Street, and Colley Avenue shall be transparent from the street.
Parking Location and Access
Where the front building facade is built within 10 feet of the front
property line of 21st Street or 22nd Street, off-street parking shall be
located behind the building(s). In addition:
One curb cut is permitted, which shall not exceed 20 feet in width.
Rear entrances to the building(s) shall be provided.
Where the building is located perpendicular to the street and faces a
parking lot, the new parking lot shall have no more than two curb cuts
not exceeding 20 feet in width. In addition:
A hedge three feet in height shall be located along the 21st Street
property line and the parking lot.
No parking or on-site circulation shall be permitted between the
building and the 21st Street property line.
Off-street Loading
No off-street loading berth shall be located on 21st Street or Colley Avenue.
Drive-through Facilities
Access to drive-through facilities shall be incorporated into allowed curb
cuts for parking, wherever feasible.
One additional curb cut for access to 21st Street or Colley Avenue may
be installed at a width no greater than 10 feet, provided it does not
impact traffic flow on the adjoining street.
Landscaping and Buffering
Except where precluded by the provisions of this district, the landscaping
and buffering standards applicable to commercial uses in Section 5.2,
Landscaping Standards, shall apply.
Signs
Sign standards for commercial establishments in Section 5.7, Signs, shall
apply, subject to the following limitations:
Establishments having 100 feet or more of lot frontage may have only
one monument type sign not to exceed 32 square feet of sign surface
area per sign face. The maximum height of the sign shall be six feet.
Establishments having 100 feet or more of lot frontage, which includes a
parking lot or parking court abutting the principal street, may have one
freestanding center identification sign or directory sign with a height

3.9.12 PCO-21st Street: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-21st Street

that does not exceed 6 feet, with up to two faces, and a sign surface
that does not exceed 20 square feet per face.
Only one A-frame sign may be placed on a public sidewalk in front of a
business, which shall be removed from the public right-of-way during
non-business hours. It shall be subject to any other conditions specified
by the ZA, to ensure it is designed and located to maintain the character
of the district.
Temporary balloons are prohibited.
Wall signs shall comply with the following standards:
They shall complement the building's architecture, materials, and
colors.
One square foot of sign surface area is allowed for each foot of
building frontage facing the public street on which principal access
is located.
One-half square foot of sign surface area is allowed for each foot of
building frontage facing other streets.
Wall signs may include, but are not limited to, the following
features:
(A) Individual articulated letters;
(B) Painted signs (on the building or on other suitable surface);
(C) Neon tubing; and
(D) Lettering on an awning.
Box wall signs, which are geometric in form, plastic coated,
internally lighted, and have a changeable face for each subsequent
tenant, are prohibited.
Digital window signage shall be permitted subject to the following
limitations:
Notwithstanding any other provisions of this subsection, the
transparency required in Section 3.9.12.C(2), Façade Treatment,
must be maintained;
One digital window sign may be permitted per storefront facing a
street. One additional digital window sign may be permitted for
any storefront fronting more than 100 linear feet on a public
street;
Signage shall be no larger than nine square feet;
Signage shall be installed a minimum of three feet off the ground
and no higher than nine feet from the ground;
Display must stay on screen a minimum of 10 seconds and can
change only by fading to the new display;

Display cannot flash, or give the appearance of flashing;
Display may be interactive, but cannot scroll or move unless being
manipulated by a user standing in front of the display;
If digital window signage is used, no temporary window signage
shall be permitted;
No exterior sound shall be emitted from the sign;
Digital window signage shall not cause glare or be lit in a way that
causes a distraction to vehicular traffic; and
No content on the digital widow sign shall be legible from the
vehicular travel lanes of adjacent streets.
Parking Standards
Off-street parking shall comply with Table 3.9.12, Off-street Parking

3.9.13 PCO-Riverview: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-Riverview

sections.title: PCO-Riverview: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay- Riverview
sections.text:
RIVERVIEW
PURPOSE
The purpose of the Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-Riverview (PCO-Riverview)
district is to maintain and enhance the commercial vitality and walkable character
of the Granby Street business area. District standards accommodate development
that supports the district’s character and planned public improvements.
APPLICABILITY
The standards and requirements in this section apply to development in the PCO-
Riverview district.
STANDARDS APPLICABLE TO DEVEL OPMENT IN THE PC O-
RIVERVIEW DISTRICT
Building Location and Orientation
A building developed on a lot abutting Granby Street shall be oriented in one
of the following configurations:
The entire front building façade shall be located 10 feet from the front
property line. Primary entrances shall be on Granby Street; or
The building orientation shall be perpendicular to Granby Street with its
principal facade and entrances facing a pedestrian plaza or parking
court. In addition, the ends of the building shall be located within 10
feet from the front property line and shall have active uses and
entrances along Granby Street.
In no case shall the building be located in the middle or rear of the lot
with parking or on-site vehicular circulation located between the
building and the property line along Granby Street.
Fenestration
A minimum of 50 percent of the ground floor facade along Granby Street
shall be transparent from the street.
Window Transparency
During all hours of business operation, all glass portions of windows and
doors along the front façade shall be maintained as transparent, as defined
in Section 8.3.2, Terms Defined, and shall not be obscured with blinds or
curtains, except those necessary to block active sunlight.
Parking Location and Access
Where the front building facade is built to or within 10 feet of the front
property line of Granby Street, off-street parking shall be provided
behind the building(s). In addition:

One curb cut on Granby Street is permitted, that does not exceed
20 feet in width.
Rear entrances to the building(s) shall be provided.
In instances where the building is located perpendicular to Granby
Street and faces a parking court, the parking lot shall have no more than
two curb cuts not exceeding 20 feet in width. In addition,
A wall or hedge three in height shall be located between the
Granby Street property and the parking lot.
No parking or on-site vehicular circulation shall be permitted
between the building and the Granby Street property line.
Off-street Loading
No off-street loading berth shall be located on Granby Street.
Drive-through Facilities
Access to drive-through facilities shall be incorporated into allowed curb
cuts for parking, wherever feasible.
One additional curb cut may be installed up to 10 feet in width,
provided it does not impact traffic flow on the adjoining street.
Landscaping and Buffering
Except where precluded by the provisions of this district, the landscaping
and buffering standards applicable to commercial uses in Section 5.2,
Landscaping Standards, shall apply.
Signs
Sign standards for commercial establishments in Section 5.7, Signs, shall
apply, subject to the limitations below.
Monument Signs
Establishments with 125 feet or more of lot frontage and a parking
area located to the front or side of the principal building may have
one monument sign facing the principal street. In addition:
(A) The sign’s face may not exceed 32 square feet of surface area.
(B) The maximum height shall be six feet from the ground to the
top of the sign.
(C) The sign shall be set back a minimum of five feet from the
public right-of-way.
A-frame Signs
One A-frame sign on a public sidewalk in front of a business is allowed,
but shall be removed from the public right-of-way during non-business
hours.

3.9.14 PCO-35th Street: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-35th Street

Balloon Signs
Temporary balloons signs are prohibited.
Wall Signs
One square foot of sign surface area is allowed for each foot of
building frontage facing the public street on which principal access
is located.
One-half square foot of sign surface area is allowed for each foot of
building frontage facing other streets.
Parking Standards
Off-street parking shall comply with Table 3.9.13, Off-street Parking
Standards.

sections.text:
35 T H STREET
PURPOSE
The purpose of the Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-35th Street (PCO-35th Street)
district is to maintain and enhance the commercial vitality and walkable character

3.9.14 PCO-35th Street: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-35th Street

of the 35th Street business area. District standards accommodate development
that supports the district’s character and planned public improvements.
APPLICABILITY
The standards and requirements in this section apply to all development in the
PCO-35th Street district.
STANDARDS APPLICABLE TO DEVEL OPMENT IN THE PC O-
35 T H STREET DISTRICT
Building Location and Orientation
A building developed on a lot abutting 35th Street shall be oriented in one of
the following configurations:
The entire front building facade shall be located between the property
line along 35th Street, and five feet from the property line. The primary
entrances to such buildings shall be on 35th Street; or
The building orientation shall be perpendicular to 35th Street with its
principal facade and entrances facing a pedestrian plaza or parking

property line along 35th Street and five feet from the property line, and

In no case shall the building be located in the middle or rear of the lot
with parking or on-site vehicular circulation between the building and
the 35th Street property line.

A minimum of 50 percent of the ground floor facade along 35th Street shall
be transparent from the street.
Parking Location and Access
Where the front building facade is built to or within five feet of the front
property line of 35th Street, off-street parking shall be provided behind
the building(s). In addition:
One curb cut is permitted on 35th Street, that does not exceed 20

Rear entrances to the building(s) shall be provided.
Where a building is located perpendicular to 35th Street and faces a
parking lot, the new parking lot shall have no more than two curb cuts
not exceeding 20 feet in width. In addition:
A wall or hedge three feet in height shall be located between the
35th Street property line and the parking lot.
No parking or on-site vehicular circulation shall be permitted
between the building and the 35th Street property line.

3.9.14 PCO-35th Street: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-35th Street

Off-street loading
No off-street loading berth shall be located on 35th Street.
Landscaping and buffering
Except where precluded by the provisions of this district, the landscaping
and buffering standards applicable to commercial uses in Section 5.2,

by the ZA, to ensure it is designed and located to maintain the character
of the district.
Temporary balloons are prohibited.
Wall signs are subject to the following:
One square foot of sign surface area is allowed for each foot of
building frontage facing the public street on which principal access

One-half square foot of sign surface area is allowed for each foot of

sections.title: PCO-Lafayette: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay- Lafayette Boulevard
sections.text:
LAFAYETTE BOULEVARD
PURPOSE
The purpose of the Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-Lafayette Boulevard (PCO-
Lafayette) district is to support the Fairmount Park neighborhood by allowing
neighborhood-serving commercial establishments. District standards
accommodate pedestrian-oriented development in the commercial nodes along
Lafayette Boulevard between Tidewater Drive and Chesapeake Boulevard.
APPLICABILITY
The standards and requirements in this section apply to all development in the
PCO-Lafayette district.
STANDARDS APPLICABLE TO DEVEL OPMENT IN THE PC O-
LAFAYETTE DISTRI CT
Standards Applicable to Development in the PCO-Lafayette District
Development in the PCO-Lafayette district shall comply with the following
standards:
Building Location and Orientation
The front building facade shall be located between five feet and 10
feet from the principal street; and
It shall occupy, in combination with plazas, courtyards, and
pedestrian corridors, at least 75 percent of the lot frontage.
Parking Location and Access
Parking lots shall not be located between the primary building and
Lafayette Boulevard or Tidewater Drive.

3.9.15 PCO-Lafayette: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-Lafayette Boulevard

Fenestration
For commercial buildings along Lafayette Boulevard or Tidewater Drive,
a minimum of 50 percent of the total area of ground floor facade shall
be transparent from the street.
Off-street Loading
An off-street loading berth shall not be located on Lafayette Boulevard
or Tidewater Drive.
Signs
The sign standards in Section 5.7, Signs, shall apply, subject to the
following limitations.
A-frame Signs
Only one A-frame sign shall be placed on a public sidewalk in front
of a business. The sign shall be removed from the public right-of-
way during non-business hours.
Pole and Pylon Signs
Poles and pylon signs are prohibited.
Monument Signs
Establishments with 100 feet or more of lot frontage may have one
monument sign facing the principal street, subject to the following:
(A) The sign face shall not exceed 32 square feet of surface area.
(B) The maximum height shall not exceed six feet from the ground
to the top of the sign.
(C) The sign shall be set back a minimum of five feet from the
public right-of-way.
Wall Signs
Wall signs shall comply with the following:
(A) The maximum sign surface area shall not exceed one square
foot of sign surface area for each linear foot of building
frontage that faces the public street and provides primary site
access.
(B) The maximum allowed wall sign surface area shall not exceed
(C) For all other building frontage, the maximum sign surface area
shall not exceed one-half square foot of sign surface area for
each linear foot of building frontage facing the public street.

3.9.15 PCO-Lafayette: Pedestrian Commercial Overlay-Lafayette Boulevard

Projecting Signs
Projecting signs are permitted, and must comply with the
following:
(A) The maximum sign surface area shall not exceed the standard
provided in Section 5.7, Signs;
(B) The sign shall not extend more than six feet from the wall of
the building; and
(C) The sign may not exceed one and one-half feet in height or
four feet in width.
Box Signs
Box signs, regardless of whether they are attached to a wall, are
prohibited.
Window Signs
(D) Signs on storefront glass shall be painted upon the glass, and
shall not exceed eight inches in height.
(E) Paper signs attached to the glass are prohibited.
Awning Signs
Signs displayed on awnings shall be restricted to the vertical drop
and may not exceed eight inches in height.
Sign Band
A single, external sign band may be applied to the façade of a
building between the first and the second floors.
Balloon Signs
Balloon signs, including temporary balloons, are not permitted.
Parking Standards
Off-street parking shall comply with Table 3.9.15, Off-street Parking
Standards.
